newsitem.title: CHINA: Hong Kong gold ends down, hit by producer sales.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong gold ends down, hit by producer sales.

text.p: Hong Kong spot gold ended down from New York's previous close on steady selling in Asian trade, some of which was producer selling, dealers said on Tuesday.
Bullion ended at US$317.50/318.00 on Tuesday, compared to New York's previous close at US$318.20/70 on Monday.
Dealers said the market traded within a broad, three-dollar range, but that was not unusual after a steep fall.
"There's no particular direction at the moment," said one bullion dealer.
The market bounced back at midday on a bout of shortcovering and physical buying, but gains were erased by afternoon selling, dealers said.
Traders reported selling from Australia at between $318 and $319 per ounce, and said that good resistence was still met at $320 per ounce.
"There's going to have to be a lot of buying before gold crosses up over that level," said another bullion source.
Local tael gold ended HK$8 down at HK$2,946.
The carry over charge at the Chinese Gold and Silver Exchange Society rose to nil from its previous fix at -5.00.
